Your responsibility

You decide how to use what the tools produce. Review and test results before relying on them, especially generated router configuration, subnet plans and queue or burst settings: try them in a lab or a maintenance window first, and keep backups of anything you change.

Lawful and authorized use

Use the security, OSINT and analysis tools (such as PCAP analysis, IOC extraction, domain and IP lookups, subdomain discovery and the decoding and cipher tools) only on systems, networks and data you own or are explicitly authorized to analyze, and in line with the laws, contracts and policies that apply to you. Don't use the toolkit to harm, disrupt or gain unauthorized access to anyone's systems.

Third-party services

Online tools send the values you look up straight from your browser to public services, including Cloudflare and Google DNS-over-HTTPS, rdap.org and the regional internet registries, RIPEstat, PeeringDB, ipwho.is, ipapi.co, crt.sh, CertSpotter, ipify and maclookup.app. Each tool says which services it uses. Those services have their own terms and privacy policies, may limit or change access without notice, and their data may be incomplete or wrong. NetOps Toolkit has no control over them.

Privacy

There is no backend and no analytics. Offline tools process everything inside your browser. Recently used tools, saved inputs, history, split-view layouts and your acceptance of this disclaimer are stored only in your browser's local storage on this device. You can turn history off or clear it from any tool's History menu.
